rows.name: Manage AI Agent Service Access
rows.quote: Limit service AI agents--agents using independently assigned service or workload permissions--to explicitly authorized workflows.
area_evidence: ### Step 1 — Declare each agent identity as service or user-delegated ⚠ CRITICAL

rows.name: Manage User-Delegated AI Agent Access
rows.quote: Limit user-delegated AI agents to explicitly authorized tasks and permissions.

rows.basis: both labelers

rows.name: Enforce Access Controls for AI Agent Tools
rows.quote: Limit AI agent tool access to each caller's authorized, task-required operations and resources, including when tools are shared across agents, users, or tenants.
area_evidence: ### Step 4 — Authorize every tool call per caller inside the tool layer ⚠ CRITICAL
rows.basis: both labelers

rows.name: AI Agent Authority Expansion Controls
rows.quote: The maximum authority available to the agent should be explicitly granted prior to runtime.

rows.name: AI Agent External Resource Lifecycle Management
rows.quote: Organizations should control external resources created or acquired by AI agents during execution by treating those resources as attributable, lifecycle-managed assets.

rows.name: Restrict AI Agent Tool Invocation on Untrusted Data
rows.quote: It is recommended that tool invocation be restricted or limited when untrusted data enters the LLM's context.

rows.name: Input and Output Validation for AI Agent Components
rows.quote: Implement validation on inputs and outputs for the tools and data sources used by AI agents.
area_evidence: ### Step 3 — Validate tool arguments against a schema before execution
### Step 4 — Validate and sanitize tool outputs and retrieved data before they re-enter the context
rows.basis: both labelers

rows.name: AI Agent Scope Drift Detection
rows.quote: Continuously evaluate whether an AI Agent's planned actions remain consistent with its current authorized objective throughout execution.
area_evidence: ### Step 5 — Check each planned action against the authorized objective
rows.basis: both labelers

rows.name: Memory Hardening
rows.quote: Record the source of all memory updates and preserve a history with known good versions. Quarantine or roll-back suspicious records.
area_evidence: ### Step 6 — If the agent has persistent memory: harden what gets written and recalled
rows.basis: adjudicated: both labelers; quote changed from the second labeler's access-control sentence (Step 6 filters by tenant and user but does not authenticate memory operations) to the provenance sentence, which Step 6 does exactly (source per write, versions, quarantine, rollback). Conditional step: applies only to agents with persistent memory.

rows.name: Generative AI Guardrails
rows.quote: Tool and action guardrails: Validate tool calls, tool arguments, permissions, and tool outputs before execution or before results are returned to the model.
area_evidence: ### Step 2 — Restrict tool invocation while untrusted data is in context ⚠ CRITICAL
### Step 3 — Validate tool arguments against a schema before execution
### Step 4 — Validate and sanitize tool outputs and retrieved data before they re-enter the context
rows.basis: adjudicated: Steps 2-4 gate each tool call, schema-validate arguments before execution and sanitize tool outputs before they re-enter the context, which is this sentence for its named object (tool calls, arguments, outputs). Only the tool/action guardrail bullet is claimed, not input/output moderation.

rows.name: Human In-the-Loop for AI Agent Actions
rows.quote: Systems should require the user or another human stakeholder to approve AI agent actions before the agent takes them.
area_evidence: ### Step 2 — Restrict tool invocation while untrusted data is in context ⚠ CRITICAL
rows.basis: adjudicated: Step 2 blocks always_approve (high-consequence) tools and tainted side-effect tools unless approval_granted comes from the approval service, so the action cannot run before a human approves. The approval UI itself is in human-oversight; in part only.

rows.name: AI Agent Authority Expansion Controls
rows.quote: Additional resources, identities, services, and targets discovered during execution should be treated as outside the authorized boundary unless they are independently validated and added to scope.
area_evidence: ### Step 5 — Check each planned action against the authorized objective
rows.basis: adjudicated: Step 5 treats any resource outside the recorded allowed set, any new party and any credential/permission-changing step as drift: calls are denied and a human must resume. That is this sentence for discovered targets. The pre-runtime authority grant is cited on agent-permissions, not here.

rows.name: Limit AI Workload Resource Consumption
rows.quote: Agentic AI systems should limit iterations, retries, tool calls, parallel tasks, delegation depth, and downstream spending.
area_evidence: ### Step 5 — Check each planned action against the authorized objective
rows.basis: adjudicated: only a per-task step budget used as a drift signal; no retry, parallelism, delegation-depth, time or spend limits, and the area lists rate limits as not covered. Citing resource-consumption limits would overclaim.

rows.name: Excessive Agency
